# 12-Week Cycle-Phased Strength Programme

**Client:** 28F, recreational lifter, severe primary dysmenorrhea
**Programme start:** 2026-06-01 (Monday)
**Cycle reference:** 28-day, last period 2026-05-01
**Flow-day restrictions:** no high-intensity, no heavy Valsalva (cap RPE 6, no maximal bracing), no jumping/impact

## Cycle Mapping Across the 12 Weeks

Using a 28-day cycle starting 2026-05-01, predicted bleed days (flow days 1–3) and rough phase windows for the programme:

| Cycle # | Flow days (debilitating, 1–3) | Follicular (days 4–13) | Ovulation (day 14) | Luteal (days 15–28) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | May 29 – May 31 | Jun 1 – Jun 10 | Jun 11 | Jun 12 – Jun 25 |
| 3 | Jun 26 – Jun 28 | Jun 29 – Jul 8 | Jul 9 | Jul 10 – Jul 23 |
| 4 | Jul 24 – Jul 26 | Jul 27 – Aug 5 | Aug 6 | Aug 7 – Aug 20 |
| 5 | Aug 21 – Aug 23 | Aug 24 – Aug 23 onward | — | — |

So within the 12-week window (Jun 1 – Aug 23), the **debilitating flow windows fall on**:
- **Week 4:** Fri Jun 26 – Sun Jun 28
- **Week 8:** Fri Jul 24 – Sun Jul 26
- **Week 12:** Fri Aug 21 – Sun Aug 23

Programme her three "Deload / Flow-Accommodation" weeks intentionally around these dates. Convenient: each falls in the final week of a four-week block, so the model is **3 weeks build → 1 week flow-accommodation deload**, repeated three times. Track her actual cycle weekly and shift sessions ±2 days if her bleed comes early/late.

---

## Programme Structure

**Frequency:** 4 days/week — Upper/Lower split (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri)
**Flow week:** sessions become Mon, Wed, Fri "Restorative" days; Thu/Fri may be skipped or kept light per symptoms.
**Loading model:** linear progression within each 3-week build, RPE-capped on flow days.

### Phase 1 — Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
Goal: re-groove patterns, build work capacity, establish baseline e1RMs on squat, bench, deadlift, OHP, RDL.

**Lower A (Mon)**
- Back squat — 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Romanian deadlift — 3×8 @ RPE 7
- Walking lunge — 3×10/leg
- Leg curl — 3×12
- Side plank — 3×30s/side

**Upper A (Tue)**
- Bench press — 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Chest-supported row — 4×8
- Seated DB shoulder press — 3×10
- Lat pulldown — 3×12
- Face pull — 3×15

**Lower B (Thu)**
- Trap-bar deadlift — 4×5 @ RPE 7
- Front-foot-elevated split squat — 3×8/leg
- Hip thrust — 3×10
- Calf raise — 3×12
- Dead bug — 3×10

**Upper B (Fri)**
- Overhead press — 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Pull-up or assisted — 4×AMRAP (stop 1 shy)
- Incline DB press — 3×10
- Single-arm row — 3×10/side
- Curl + triceps superset — 3×12

**Week 1 (Jun 1–7):** Introduce loads, leave 2-3 reps in reserve. Cycle day 32 → already in next follicular phase — strong week, push intent slightly.
**Week 2 (Jun 8–14):** Add 2.5–5 kg compounds where rep quality held. Ovulation mid-week.
**Week 3 (Jun 15–21):** Top loading week of block; early luteal, energy still good. RPE 8 allowable on top sets.
**Week 4 (Jun 22–28) — Flow-accommodation deload:**
- Mon Jun 22, Tue Jun 23: normal sessions but drop to 60% of Week 3 loads, RPE 6.
- Wed Jun 24, Thu Jun 25: PMS likely — light mobility + Z2 walk 30 min.
- **Fri Jun 26 – Sun Jun 28 (bleed days 1–3): NO training in the gym.** Replace with **Restorative Protocol** (see below).

---

### Phase 2 — Hypertrophy / Strength Build (Weeks 5–8)
Goal: accumulate volume in follicular and ovulatory windows where she'll feel strongest; manage luteal fatigue.

Same split, increased volume. Substitute the main lifts' top set with a back-off cluster.

**Lower A**
- Back squat — 4×5 @ RPE 8, then 2×8 @ ~70%
- RDL — 4×8
- Bulgarian split squat — 3×8/leg
- Leg curl — 4×10
- Pallof press — 3×10/side

**Upper A**
- Bench — 4×5 @ RPE 8, then 2×8 @ ~70%
- Pendlay row — 4×6
- Seated DB OHP — 4×8
- Lat pulldown — 3×10
- Cable fly + tri pushdown superset — 3×12

**Lower B**
- Trap-bar DL — 4×4 @ RPE 8
- Hip thrust — 4×8
- Reverse lunge — 3×10/leg
- Calf raise — 4×10
- Bird-dog — 3×8/side

**Upper B**
- OHP — 4×5 @ RPE 8
- Weighted pull-up / lat pulldown — 4×6
- Incline DB press — 3×10
- Chest-supported row — 3×12
- Arms finisher — 3×12

**Week 5 (Jun 29 – Jul 5):** Post-bleed follicular — push hardest sessions Tue/Thu, expect PRs on rep targets.
**Week 6 (Jul 6–12):** Ovulation Thu Jul 9 — possible peak strength but also slight joint laxity; keep tempo controlled on squats/lunges.
**Week 7 (Jul 13–19):** Mid-luteal. Energy may dip, sleep worsens. Maintain loads but allow 1 extra rest day if needed; cut accessory volume by one set if RPE creeps.
**Week 8 (Jul 20–26) — Flow-accommodation deload:**
- Mon Jul 20, Tue Jul 21: 60% loads, RPE 6, full warm-up emphasis.
- Wed Jul 22, Thu Jul 23: skip or mobility-only.
- **Fri Jul 24 – Sun Jul 26 (bleed):** Restorative Protocol.

---

### Phase 3 — Strength Expression (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: heavier intensities (singles, doubles, triples), test e1RMs end of block.

**Lower A**
- Back squat — work to top triple @ RPE 8, then 3×3 @ 90% of top
- RDL — 3×6
- Walking lunge — 3×8/leg
- Leg curl — 3×10
- Side plank — 3×40s/side

**Upper A**
- Bench — top triple @ RPE 8, then 3×3 @ 90%
- Chest-supported row — 4×6
- Seated OHP — 3×6
- Pulldown — 3×10
- Face pull — 3×15

**Lower B**
- Trap-bar DL — work to top double @ RPE 8, then 2×3
- Hip thrust — 4×6
- Split squat — 3×6/leg
- Calf raise — 3×10
- Dead bug — 3×10

**Upper B**
- OHP — top triple @ RPE 8, then 3×3
- Weighted pull-up — 4×4
- Incline DB press — 3×8
- Row — 3×10
- Arms — 3×12

**Week 9 (Jul 27 – Aug 2):** Follicular — best intensity week. Hit top triples confidently.
**Week 10 (Aug 3–9):** Ovulation Aug 6 — biggest lifts of the block likely land here; supervise bracing.
**Week 11 (Aug 10–16):** Luteal. Hold intensity but reduce accessory volume 20%.
**Week 12 (Aug 17–23) — Flow-accommodation + test:**
- Mon Aug 17: Squat e1RM test (work to heavy triple, calculate). She's still pre-bleed — fine.
- Tue Aug 18: Bench e1RM test.
- Wed Aug 19: Deadlift e1RM test.
- Thu Aug 20: OHP e1RM test + light row work.
- **Fri Aug 21 – Sun Aug 23 (bleed):** Restorative Protocol, no testing.

If her bleed arrives earlier than expected, **shift testing forward** and abort any session at first sign of cramping/onset.

---

## Flow-Day Restorative Protocol (used on every predicted bleed day across the 12 weeks)

Per GP clearance: no high-intensity, no Valsalva, no jumping. The aim is symptom relief and maintaining the training habit, not adaptation.

**Daily option (20–35 min, client's choice based on symptom severity):**
- 5–10 min easy walking or stationary bike (very low resistance) — gentle aerobic activity has good evidence for reducing dysmenorrhea pain.
- Cat-cow ×10
- Child's pose 60s
- Supine figure-4 stretch 60s/side
- Happy baby 60s
- Supported bridge with pillow under sacrum 2 min
- Diaphragmatic (belly) breathing 5 min — emphasise long exhales; explicitly **no breath-holding or bracing**.
- Optional: gentle bodyweight glute bridge 2×10 (no load, nasal breathing only) if she feels up to it.

**If pain is severe (debilitating day 1):** skip entirely. Heat pack + rest is the intervention. Reassure her this is programmed, not lost progress.

---

## Recovery & Lifestyle Anchors (12-week constants)

- **Sleep:** 7.5–9 h. Particularly emphasise the 3 nights before predicted bleed — poor sleep amplifies prostaglandin-driven cramping.
- **Z2 cardio:** 2 × 30 min/week (walk, cycle, swim), on off days. Skip on bleed days unless gentle walking helps.
- **Hydration:** 2.5–3 L/day, more in luteal phase (water retention is normal — don't restrict).
- **Magnesium:** discuss with GP; magnesium glycinate 200–300 mg/day in luteal phase has modest evidence for cramp reduction.
- **Omega-3:** 1–2 g EPA+DHA/day — some RCT evidence for primary dysmenorrhea symptom reduction over 2–3 cycles.
- **NSAID timing (her GP's call):** if she uses ibuprofen/naproxen, taking it **prophylactically 1–2 days before expected bleed** is more effective than waiting for pain — flag this for her to discuss at next GP visit.
- **Caffeine:** keep <200 mg/day in late luteal/bleed week if she finds it worsens cramps.

---

## Nutrition Notes

I'd want her bodyweight, goals, and current intake to programme calories/macros properly, but as a default for a 28F recreational lifter on a strength block:

- **Protein:** 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day, spread across 4 meals.
- **Carbs:** prioritise around training, especially follicular/ovulation windows when she's pushing intensity. Don't drop carbs in luteal — cravings and worse mood/cramps tend to follow.
- **Iron:** heavy flow days mean iron loss. Include iron-rich foods (red meat, lentils, dark leafy greens with vitamin C source) across the cycle. Worth asking her GP about ferritin levels given she describes flow days as debilitating — low iron is common and worsens both training and dysmenorrhea symptoms.
- **Slight caloric surplus** (~150–250 kcal) during build weeks 1–3, 5–7, 9–11; maintenance during deload/flow weeks.

---

## Tracking & Decision Rules

1. **Log actual cycle day** at every session. If her bleed shifts by >2 days, slide the deload week to match.
2. **Symptom flag:** if she reports cramping mid-session, end the session — no Valsalva, no finishers.
3. **Two cycles in (end of Week 8)**, review whether the 3:1 build:deload rhythm is matching her symptom pattern. Some clients benefit from also pulling intensity (not just on bleed days) in the 2–3 days pre-bleed; if her PMS is significant, we'd shift to a luteal-taper model in cycles 3.
4. **Re-test e1RMs** Week 12. Expect 5–10% gains on upper lifts, 7–12% on lower if adherence is good.

Let me know her bodyweight, current lifts (or estimated 1RMs), training history specifics, and any equipment constraints, and I'll tighten the load prescriptions.

# Cycle-Phased Nutrition Plan

To prescribe specific calories I need her bodyweight, height, and activity outside training — but here's a complete framework you can scale. I've built it for a **~65 kg recreational lifter** as a working example; adjust proportionally.

## Baseline Targets (working example: 65 kg)

- **Maintenance:** ~2,200 kcal/day
- **Protein:** 1.8 g/kg = **120 g/day** (anchor — keep constant across the cycle)
- **Fats:** 0.8–1.0 g/kg = **55–65 g/day**
- **Carbs:** the variable lever — adjusted by cycle phase (see below)
- **Fibre:** 28–35 g/day
- **Fluids:** 2.5–3 L/day baseline, +500 ml on training days, +500 ml in late luteal/bleed

---

## Phase-by-Phase Nutrition (28-day cycle)

### Follicular Phase (Days 4–13) — "Push Phase"
Best insulin sensitivity, lowest core temp, highest training capacity. Match the fuelling to the work.

- **Calories:** maintenance + 200 (build weeks)
- **Carbs:** **4–5 g/kg** (~260–325 g) — load these around training
- **Fats:** moderate (55 g)
- **Iron focus:** this is the recovery-from-bleed window. Push iron intake hard.
  - Red meat 2–3×/week, or
  - Lentils/chickpeas/tofu + vitamin C source (peppers, citrus, strawberries) at the same meal to boost non-haem iron absorption
  - Avoid tea/coffee within 1 hour of iron-rich meals (tannins block absorption)
- **Sample pre-training meal (1–2 h before):** oats 80 g + whey 30 g + berries + 1 tbsp almond butter

### Ovulation (Day 14) — "Peak Output"
Strength may peak; also slight joint laxity. Fuel fully.

- **Calories:** maintenance + 200
- **Carbs:** **5 g/kg** on the heavy session day
- Add **electrolytes intra-workout** (500 ml water + 300–500 mg sodium) — basal temp rising means slightly higher sweat losses.

### Early Luteal (Days 15–21) — "Maintain"
Resting metabolic rate rises ~5–10% (roughly 100–150 extra kcal/day). Cravings are physiological, not weakness.

- **Calories:** maintenance + 250–350 (don't restrict — undereating here amplifies PMS and worsens next bleed)
- **Carbs:** **3.5–4.5 g/kg**, weighted toward complex sources (oats, rice, potato, quinoa, fruit)
- **Protein:** consider nudging up to 2.0 g/kg — satiety + amino acid demand both rise
- **Magnesium:** **300 mg glycinate** with evening meal (start Day 15) — evidence for cramp reduction over consecutive cycles
- **B6:** 50–100 mg/day from Day 15 to Day 1 — modest evidence for PMS mood/bloating
- **Dark chocolate (70%+):** legitimate — magnesium + small dopamine bump. 20–30 g/day fits the plan.

### Late Luteal (Days 22–28) — "Anti-Inflammatory / Cramp Prep"
This is where prostaglandin production ramps up. Nutrition here directly affects how bad days 1–3 will be.

- **Calories:** maintenance + 200
- **Carbs:** **3.5–4 g/kg**, complex sources, evenly distributed (helps mood + sleep via serotonin)
- **Omega-3 emphasis:** 2 g EPA+DHA/day — oily fish (salmon, sardines, mackerel) 2× this week, plus supplement if needed. Omega-3s competitively inhibit the arachidonic acid → prostaglandin pathway that drives her cramping.
- **Reduce omega-6 load:** less seed oil, fried food, ultra-processed snacks this week — these feed the same pathway in the wrong direction.
- **Anti-inflammatory additions:**
  - Ginger 1–2 g/day (fresh in tea, or capsules) — meta-analyses show effect comparable to ibuprofen for primary dysmenorrhea pain when started 1–2 days pre-bleed
  - Turmeric + black pepper with meals
  - Tart cherry juice 30 ml/day — improves sleep quality
- **Cap caffeine at 200 mg** (one coffee) — vasoconstriction can worsen cramping
- **Reduce alcohol to near-zero** — worsens sleep, water retention, PMS
- **Salt:** don't aggressively cut. Modest sodium with high water intake reduces bloating better than restriction does.

### Flow Days 1–3 (Debilitating Window) — "Comfort + Replenishment"
She likely won't want to eat much on Day 1. Prioritise tolerability over hitting macros perfectly.

- **Calories:** maintenance (don't push surplus, don't deficit)
- **Protein anchor:** still aim for 1.6 g/kg minimum — easy sources: Greek yogurt, whey shakes, eggs, soup with shredded chicken
- **Carbs:** keep up — low intake worsens cramps and mood. Easy-to-eat options: rice porridge, banana, toast with honey, oat-based smoothies

  - Day 1–3: include haem iron source daily if tolerable (eggs, chicken thigh, beef)
  - If vegetarian: lentils + vitamin C; consider checking ferritin with GP
- **Hydration:** add electrolytes (sodium + potassium + magnesium) — 1–2 servings/day. Helps headaches and fatigue.
- **Warm foods/drinks:** ginger tea, bone broth, soups — symptomatic comfort, and ginger keeps working
- **Avoid:** high-fat fried meals (slow gastric emptying, worsen nausea), excess caffeine, alcohol, very cold drinks (some clients report worse cramping)
- **If appetite is gone Day 1:** liquid calories are fine — smoothie with whey, banana, oats, milk, peanut butter, frozen berries, ginger = ~600 kcal, 35 g protein, complete

## Modality Selection

Pick **low-impact, low-skill** options. She's already squatting heavy on Mondays and the goal is metabolic stress without adding orthopaedic load or compromising next-week's lifts.

**Preferred:**
- **Assault bike / Echo bike** — best option; self-limiting, full-body, no impact

- Running sprints (impact + eccentric leg load)

If access is limited and the bike is the only option, that's fine — variety isn't needed for a once-weekly dose.

## HIIT Protocols by Phase

### Phase 1 — Introduction (Weeks 1–3)

**Format: 30-second efforts, 90-second recovery (1:3 work:rest)**

This is the gentlest true-HIIT format. Long recoveries let her hit each effort with quality and keep cardiac drift modest.

- **Week 1:** 6 rounds × (30 s hard / 90 s easy) on assault bike. Total work: 3 min. Session: ~15 min including warm-up/cooldown.
- **Week 2:** 7 rounds
- **Week 3:** 8 rounds

**Effort target:** RPE 8 on first round, RPE 9 by final round. HR should reach 85–90% max (~165–175 bpm) on later intervals. If she can't get HR up by round 3, she's pacing too conservatively.

### Phase 2 — Build (Weeks 5–6)

**Format mix: keep the 30/90, add one session of 40/80**

- **Week 5:** 8 rounds × (30 s / 90 s)
- **Week 6:** 6 rounds × (40 s / 80 s) — same total work, denser, higher cardiac demand. **This is the hardest HIIT session of the programme.** Schedule it Saturday Jul 11 (just after ovulation, two days after Thu deadlift — most recovered slot).

### Phase 3 — Polish (Weeks 9–10)

**Format: introduce shorter, harder VO2-style intervals**

- **Week 9:** 5 rounds × (60 s hard / 2 min easy) — Norwegian 4x4 style, slightly shorter. RPE 8.5 sustained.
- **Week 10:** 4 rounds × (4 min Z4 / 3 min easy) — proper VO2max intervals. This overlaps with the Z4 dose already in Wednesday's Week 11 cardio session, so **swap them**: do the 4×4 on Saturday Aug 8 instead of Wednesday Aug 12. Avoids stacking high-intensity in luteal.

## Standing Session Structure

Every HIIT session:

1. **Warm-up (8–10 min):** 5 min Z1 → 3 min Z2 → 2× (20 s @ 70% effort, 40 s easy)
2. **Work intervals** (per protocol above)
3. **Cooldown (5 min):** Z1 spin until HR < 120 bpm, then 2 min walking
4. **Mobility (5 min):** hip flexor stretch, pigeon, child's pose

Total time: ~25–35 min depending on phase.

## Cycle-Specific Cues

- **Follicular HIIT (Weeks 1, 5, 9):** push effort, expect best output. Add 5 g carb + caffeine 60 min pre-session if she tolerates caffeine.
- **Ovulation HIIT (Weeks 2, 6, 10):** strongest sessions, but slightly elevated core temp — push hydration (extra 500 ml water + 400 mg sodium pre-session). If she's prone to mid-cycle pain (mittelschmerz), pull intensity 10%.
- **Never in late luteal:** if she insists she feels good, the answer is still no — Saturday late-luteal stays Z2. The cramp-symptom data from 2–3 cycles will validate this.

## Recovery Cost & Programme Interactions

HIIT on Saturday means:

- **Sunday Z1 walk becomes non-negotiable** (active recovery; helps clear residual fatigue). If she's wrecked, swap for 20 min mobility.
- **Monday squat session** is 48 h post-HIIT — enough recovery, but watch top-set RPE. If RPE drifts up at planned loads two weeks in a row, the HIIT is taking too much. Cut HIIT, not the squat.
- **Phase 2 Saturday HIIT (Weeks 5–6)** is the highest-risk overlap with the pushed strength intensity. If any of the Week 5–6 lifting sessions miss prescribed back-off reps, pull Week 6 HIIT and replace with Z2.

Quick layer on top of the existing nutrition plan:

- **Pre-session (60–90 min before):** 30 g carb (banana + small bowl of oats, or rice cake with honey). HIIT is glycolytic — fasted is a bad idea here, especially in any luteal-adjacent week.

- **Post:** within 60 min, hit a normal mixed meal — 30 g protein + 60+ g carbs
- **Caffeine:** 100–200 mg, 45 min pre-session, only on HIIT days and only in follicular/ovulation weeks. Skip caffeine entirely the week before bleed.

## Tracking & Cut Criteria

Watch these specifically for HIIT tolerance:

1. **HR recovery 1 min post-final interval:** should drop ≥25 bpm within a minute by Week 6. If it stalls or worsens, she's overcooked.
2. **Subjective recovery score Sunday morning (1–10):** flag anything < 6.

## Standing Plyometric Session Rules

1. **Always before fatiguing work, never after.** Plyos are CNS-demanding — they need a fresh nervous system. This is why they're pre-squat on Monday, not post.
2. **Full recovery between reps.** Not between sets — between *reps*. 10–15 s minimum between jumps. Plyometrics is not conditioning.
3. **Quality stops the set.** Any landing she can't stick (Phase 1–2) or any contact time that drags long (Phase 3) ends the set immediately.
4. **No plyos within 48 h of bleed onset.** If her cycle shifts and bleed arrives early, cancel that day's plyo work — strength session can continue at reduced intensity if she feels fine.
5. **Hard surface only if appropriate footwear.** Rubber gym floor preferred. No plyos on concrete.
6. **No plyos on consecutive days.** Mon + Sat gives 4 days between sessions — adequate.

## Cycle-Specific Plyo Cues

- **Follicular:** her best landing mechanics, best power output. Push intensity ceilings here.
- **Ovulation:** relaxin and oestrogen peak. Slight increase in ligamentous laxity is documented but the practical implication is modest — emphasise **landing alignment** verbally rather than reducing load. If she has any history of knee or ankle issues, then cut intensity 10% mid-cycle.
- **Early luteal:** fine for plyos at moderate intensity. Coordination may feel slightly off — keep volume rather than chasing PRs.
- **Late luteal:** cut volume 30–40%. Coordination, sleep, and core temp all work against quality plyo work. This is the easiest week to get hurt.
- **Flow days:** zero plyos. GP-mandated. Non-negotiable.

# 1RM Testing — Honest Assessment

Short answer: **I'd recommend against it for this client at this time.** Let me lay out the reasoning, then give you a protocol if you and she still want to proceed.

## Why I'd Push Back

**1. The Week 12 timing collides with her bleed window.**

Week 12 is Aug 17–23. Her bleed starts Aug 21 (Friday). True 1RM testing requires maximal Valsalva — the GP has explicitly restricted heavy Valsalva on flow days. That means **all 1RM attempts have to land Mon–Thu (Aug 17–20)**, and on Thu she's potentially in the 24–48 h pre-bleed window where PMS symptoms, sleep disruption, and cramping often begin.

Practically: she has 4 days to test 4 lifts, with the last one landing right when symptoms typically start ramping. That's a compressed, risk-loaded testing block.

**2. The programme wasn't built as a 1RM peaking block.**

Phase 3 as written tops out at heavy triples and doubles at RPE 8–9. That's an e1RM-test design, not a true 1RM-test design. To safely test a real 1RM, the last 2–3 weeks should taper volume aggressively, expose her to heavy singles at RPE 8 in Week 10–11, and arrive at testing fresh and grooved at >90% loads. **She won't have touched a true single in this programme.** First 1RM attempt of the block being the actual test is poor practice.

**3. She's a recreational lifter, not a competitive one.**

The information value of a true 1RM vs. an e1RM from a heavy triple is small for a recreational client. The injury risk delta is not small. e1RM from a heavy 3 at RPE 8–9 is typically within 2–3% of true 1RM and tells you everything you need for programming the next block.

**4. We've already stacked a lot.**

Phase 2 pushed intensity, plyos added, cardio base building, HIIT (then removed), nutrition load — by Week 12 she's done 11 weeks of accumulating fatigue. True 1RM testing assumes fresh, peaked athletes. She'll be neither in the strictest sense.

**5. Cycle-symptom risk.**

The single most predictable thing about heavy 1RM testing is the central nervous system cost. CNS load in the late luteal/pre-bleed window has, in some clients with severe dysmenorrhea, been associated with worsened symptoms in the imminent cycle. We don't have great RCT data on this specifically, but the mechanism is plausible (HPA axis load) and the downside (worse bleed) is exactly what she's trying to avoid.

**Test heavy triples at RPE 9, calculate e1RM.** This is what the programme as written already does in Week 12. It gives:

- 95–97% of the information of a true 1RM
- Substantially lower injury risk
- No requirement for max Valsalva
- Easier to abort an attempt that feels wrong
